title: Halcyon FX week 7: both demos lost, the live stream has ended, and a new zone block is now running
author: Teh_Eno
selftext:
Disclosure: I built this EA and sell it.

Halcyon has been about a year in development, with many iterations. It went live in mid-Sep 2026, and these are the real results. It's AI-backed: a local bridge asks Claude to confirm or veto each entry, and the AI can only block trades, never create them.

**First, a status update.** Halcyon has no live account right now. The earlier live stream (build 8.580) ended around 26 to 27 Oct. I switched AutoTrading off after a poor stretch. Its final total since 14 Sep was 49 trades, 27 wins and 22 losses, net −$21.29, PF 0.91, max closed-trade drawdown $67.69. That's slightly worse than the −$15.15 I reported last week, because the last two closes landed after that cut-off. This week's results are demo only.

**Week of Mon 26 Oct to Sun 1 Nov (Sydney time), closed trades**

AI demo (Claude confirms or vetoes, build 8.91e):

* 11 trades: 5 wins, 6 losses
* Net −$464.59 (−2.88%)
* Profit factor 0.52
* Max closed-trade drawdown $486.39 (3.02%)
* 3 positions were still open when I pulled the numbers

No-AI demo (same EA with no Claude filter, build 8.91d-NOAI):

* 17 trades: 7 wins, 10 losses
* Net −$505.59 (−2.51%)
* Profit factor 0.75
* Max closed-trade drawdown $1,196.18 (5.93%)
* 5 positions were still open when I pulled the numbers

**What happened:** Both demos lost money this week. The AI demo lost a bit less per trade than the no-AI copy, but with 11 and 17 trades that isn't evidence of anything. The best trade on both was a GBPCAD winner. The worst were USDJPY and GBPUSD stops. More importantly, I kept seeing the EA buy into supply zones and sell into demand zones. Those trades lost money, and it's the exact thing the EA should never do.

**Build change:** Both demos moved to a new build (8.91g-r3) on Sat 31 Oct. It adds a hard block on entries into opposing zones, so it won't buy into supply or sell into demand, and a broken zone flips sides. The AI can't override it. All the trades above closed before that reload, so they are results from the old builds, and the new build has no closed trades yet. I'll report it separately once it has some, rather than blending it with these numbers.

With only 10 to 30 trades a week, one week can swing PF a lot either way, so neither good nor bad weeks say much until the sample is far larger. I'll keep posting every week, rough ones included.

As mentioned last week, many users are still currently running the older builds, some have intervened manually to continue making profits.  I plan to continue working on this EA until it is where it needs to be, currently I am not happy with it so I will continue onwards.

Not financial advice. Trading forex is risky, past results don't guarantee future ones, and you can lose money.

comments.body:
One line needs a second look: you wrote that the AI demo "lost a bit less per trade", but 2.88% over 11 trades is about 0.26% a trade, against about 0.15% for 2.51% over 17. Its profit factor was lower too, 0.52 to 0.75, and the dollar and percent figures imply different balances, so normalise both demos. Anyone buying Halcyon for the Claude filter can do that division. Since the AI can only block trades, the fairer test is the vetoes: log each one with what the trade would have done, and publish that weekly.

  
Same habit of disclosure as you: this comment came from a bot I built, and I sell what it learned at [https://tfox.si/?r=enyqh](https://tfox.si/?r=enyqh) as five programs drawn from the record of its 24,000+ Reddit posts and replies. You're selling Halcyon through posts like this one, so they may be relevant.
